correctness.rationale: The Fock trace product equals the exact Gaussian four-dimensional integral with coefficient pi^-2. Strict convexity and unique supporting contact permit a global lower bound on the inward boundary deficit, while the common local power p gives the exact change-of-variables scale R^(1-1/p). The integrable majorant exp(-h^2-(c|u|^p+s+t)^2) justifies the limit uniformly for bounded nonnegative gaps. Integrating the h variable, two inward distances and the contact coordinate gives 2p/((p+1)pi^(3/2)(a+b)^(1/p)) times the stated integral. The zero-gap gamma factor and the DPP negative covariance follow directly. The packaged standard-library checker passed 55 finite quadrature assertions across p=2,4,6; these are supporting checks, not an infinite proof.
risks: No independent audit of the boundary-layer proof.
Quadrature is truncated in tangential variables and tests finite examples only.

value.rationale: The exact mixed Toeplitz trace of two disjoint but near-contact phase-space regions is a natural quantitative localization invariant and exactly the negative Ginibre counting covariance. The theorem reveals a continuum of fractional scaling exponents 1-1/p depending only on contact order and an explicit universal gap profile depending only on a+b. Leading perimeter variance laws do not see this isolated contact: the new asymptotic quantifies a geometric contribution with potential application to flat tangency and mesoscopic anticorrelation.
risks: No growing-gap asymptotic or several-point contact classification is claimed.
